newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE may drop to 4,410 trendline support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE may drop to 4,410 trendline support.

text.p: The FTSE 100 may drop back to 4,410 on Friday in an initial reaction to the resounding victory by the Labour Party in yesterday's parliamentary election, technical analysts said.

Such a move would take the index to trendline support formed by joining the FTSE's intra-day lows since April 14. There is then a risk of further deterioration and a tumble to 4,360 in stages is then possible, they added.
In the past, such sharp falls have been an opportunity to buy the market and this pattern of trading maay be repeated.
By 0840 GMT, the FTSE down 18.0 at 4,427.0.
Over the past two days, the maket has twitched nervously near its record high and reflected investor discomfort to take aggressive action ahead of the election.

Institutional investors will spend some time to adjust their portfolios in the light of a change in government and banks, utilities, healthcare and pharmaceuticals which have been leading the market higher recently will all take a knock this morning.
But an over-reaction to Labour's victory may be exploited by market bulls later this afternoon and this will depend on non-farm payroll data from the U.S. which are released at 1230 GMT.

Economists polled by Reuters expect U.S. payrolls to have gone up by 211,000 in April which will take the unemployment rate in the U.S. to 5.2 percent. They forecast average hourly earnings to have risen 0.3 percent in April.
If the payroll and earnings figures are very much larger than expected, they will rekindle inflationary fears and the U.S. and UK stock markets will go into a tailspin.
Some recovery, or even a rally, will ensue if the figures show inflation is under control, analysts said.
